summary: Dedicated pool throughput collapse: allocator holding reservations due to noisy short-stream tenant and autoscaler non-reactivity
description:
Issue summary:
Customer GreenDraft reports a sudden drop in dedicated pool throughput for their pinned redwood-7b-quantized route. Traffic shows many short, low-latency streams interleaving with medium-length requests. During the window the autoscaler did not increase GPU count and the allocator kept several reservations in a 'pending-attach' state for >10 minutes, leading to effective GPU scarcity for the tenant's steady traffic.

Impact:
- GreenDraft reported 60% reduction in sustained throughput for 40 minutes across their reserved pool; several customer operations timed out (500s) and degraded user experience.
- Other tenants in the same reserved cluster experienced elevated p99 as the allocator struggled to satisfy attach requests.

Timeline (local):
- 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC: GreenDraft support pinged #support with elevated 5xxs.
- 09:15 UTC: CS opened this ticket and collected traces.
- 09:20 UTC: Metrics show burst of short-stream connections from tenant T-1427 and repeated prefetch attempts.
- 09:28 UTC: Autoscaler telemetry shows decision loop skipped scaling due to stale heartbeat metric from allocator (delta > 60s).
- 09:40 UTC: Several reservations in "pending-attach" for >600s; attach attempts retried but failed due to allocator-side attach backoff.

Environment:
- Dedicated reserved pool cluster: reserved-cluster-7
- Region: us-east-1
- Customer-tier: dedicated (monthly commit)
- Model pinned: redwood-7b-quantized (q4_0)

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Create mixed workload with many short live streams (<2s) interleaved with regular long requests (10-30s).
2) Issue repeated prefetch/kvcache requests from a single tenant at high fanout (~200 concurrent short streams).
3) Observe allocator reservations being created then stuck in pending-attach; autoscaler does not trigger additional GPUs until heartbeat recovers.

Observed behavior:
- Allocator holds reservations in pending state and does not release them quickly (lock-time ~10m).
- Autoscaler decision loop reports stale heartbeat (allocator.telemetry.heartbeat_lag > 60s) and suppresses scale-up to avoid thrashing.
- Small-stream tenant appears to cause kv-cache churn and ephemeral slot-locks that block larger batch assignments.

Expected behavior:
- Allocator should either free stale reservations after a short timeout or escalate attach attempts; autoscaler should consider alternative telemetry (queue depth) to trigger scale-up when heartbeat is stale.

Logs / metrics attached (excerpt):
- allocator.attach.pending_count spikes from 3 -> 42 between 09:18-09:29 UTC
- autoscaler.decision.suppressed_due_to_heartbeat_lag = true at 09:28 UTC
- gpu.attach.retry_backoff increased to 120s for several attach attempts
- kvcache.evictions per-sec elevated on nodes hosting tenant T-1427

Initial triage summary:
- Triage indicates noisy short-stream tenant causing slot fragmentation and a separate allocator heartbeat edge-case where heartbeat lag suppressed autoscaler scale-ups.
- Priority raised to P1 because this is customer-impacting on a reserved contract.

Immediate mitigations attempted:
- 09:35 UTC: Support increased per-tenant short-stream throttle for T-1427 via emergency override (reduced short-stream concurrency from ~200->40) — partial recovery in p50 but p99 remained elevated.
- 09:43 UTC: Manually cleared 18 pending reservations via allocator admin command; some slots freed and attach retried successfully.

Next steps (engineering):
- SRE to examine allocator heartbeat root cause (possible slow metric exporter on nodes) and implement temporary lower timeout for pending-attach for dedicated clusters.
- Autoscaler team to add fallback signal (queue_depth or attach_fail_rate) for scale decisions when heartbeat is stale.
- Recommend policy to rate-limit short-stream fanout per tenant for dedicated pools until a durable fix is rolled out.

investigation_notes:
Detailed findings:
- Root-cause chain appears to be: noisy tenant T-1427 opens many short streams causing high kvcache eviction and prefetch churn -> allocator creates many reservations to satisfy ephemeral attachments -> node-side attach agent experienced transient kernel driver timeouts (seen as NACKs) causing pending-attach backlog -> exporter on one allocator node lagged, marking heartbeat stale -> autoscaler suppressed scale-up.
- Reproduced in staging with synthetic short-stream generator; pending-attach timeout default (10m) too long for dedicated pools with high churn.
- Allocation logs reference kernel error codes: CU_DRIVER_TIMEOUT (sampled) and repeated socket ECONNRESET during attach handshakes.
- Related config: reserved-cluster-7 uses attach_retry.backoff=30s, pending_attach_timeout=600s.
resolution:
Temporary fixes implemented:
- Short-term: Per-tenant short-stream concurrency limit applied for GreenDraft; manual clearing of pending reservations restored baseline throughput.
- Mid-term: Reduced pending_attach_timeout from 600s -> 120s for high-churn dedicated pools (config roll-out scheduled).
- Autoscaler change: Emergency patch to consider queue_depth when heartbeat_lag detected merged to canary (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/4002).
- Infra follow-up: Allocator node agent updated to improve attach retry semantics and surface clearer metric for attach_fail_rate.

Follow-ups (action items):
- Allocator team to land more robust attach idempotency and reduce reliance on long pending timeouts (owner: Arjun Patel). Target: 2026-03-20.
- Autoscaler team to add queue-depth fallback and write integration test for heartbeat-lag scenario (owner: Lena Sørensen). Target: 2026-03-18.
- Support/Customer Success to schedule RCA call with GreenDraft and share mitigation plan and timeline.

Ticket status: In Progress (tracking remediation and customer communication).
resolution_notes: Applied config change to pending_attach_timeout and rolled autoscaler fallback to canary in us-east; monitoring shows pending_attach_count reduced by 70% and GreenDraft p50/p90 recovering to expected. Continued monitoring for 72 hours recommended.
